name: Exorbyte
tagline: German error-tolerant search and matching engine, now sold for identity resolution and data matching.
description: exorbyte is a German company that has sold a fault-tolerant search and matching engine since about 2000, originally best known for e-commerce site search and now marketed as matchmaker, an identity-resolution and explainable data-matching engine. matchmaker pulls records from an organisation's existing systems into one in-memory index and runs parallel similarity algorithms, led by Levenshtein distance and including phonetic and semantic variants in more than 30 languages, to find people, companies or addresses despite typos, swapped fields or poor data quality. It is used for duplicate prevention, address validation, KYC and sanctions screening and input management in public administration, finance, insurance and utilities, deployed on premises or as a cloud web service. It is a specialised matching index rather than a general-purpose database.

pricing.notes: Sold through demos and sales contracts; no public price list.

scale.notes: Indexes the full reference dataset in memory on 64-bit servers; vendor claims millisecond responses at big-data volumes.

strengths: Error-tolerant matching across fields: typos, phonetic variants and swapped name parts are handled
One in-memory index over several source systems, updated within milliseconds of source changes
Multilingual matching (30+ languages) with explainable match results
Packaged use cases for KYC, sanctions screening, deduplication and address checks
weaknesses: Not a system of record: it indexes data that lives elsewhere
Proprietary with no public documentation, pricing or benchmarks
Small vendor with a mainly German-speaking customer base
useCases: Duplicate detection and prevention in CRM and customer master data
Matching scanned documents to customer records during input management
